key_insight: The paper shows that replacing per-sample weights with a selection network in meta-learning for data selection requires a different objective, because the obvious formulation can destabilize training and hurt transfer.
engineering_relevance: TESS offers a scalable way to score and select training data for large language models, improving dataset curation across different data scales and model sizes.
method: Introduces Transferable Example Scoring and Selection (TESS) for data selection.
Uses a Pointwise Value Matching (PVM) objective instead of standard meta-learning losses.
Addresses weight suppression and over-reliance on easy features to improve stability and transferability.
evidence_signal: Experiments on LLM safety and targeted instruction tuning show transfer from subsets to full corpora and from smaller to larger models.
watch_item: The selection-network approach is sensitive to loss design, so direct reuse of existing MTS objectives may lead to unstable optimization and poor generalization.
paper_title: Scalable, Transferable Meta-network for Data Selection Requires a Different Loss (and Why the Obvious Choice is Problematic)
